note: Behaviour definitions for the brand-input boundary, successful derivation, and explicit refusal cases. Model-graded execution is harness scope; the deterministic derivation is covered by tests/run.sh.

evals.prompt: We have a machine-readable visual brand with a terracotta action hue, warm-tinted neutrals, white on-anchor text, a 1.25 type ratio, and a specific aesthetic commitment. Turn it into tokens.json and a four-layer DESIGN.md, then validate it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to brand-to-system, derives rather than improvises the token graph, records measured Layer-4 relationships, and requires a strict validator pass.
expectations: Uses brand-to-system because a machine-readable visual brand is the input, rather than authoring a system from intent alone.
Derives the primary against its on-anchor label before dependent tokens commit.
Produces tokens.json and a four-layer DESIGN.md whose Layer 4 contains computed relationships.
Runs the sibling validate-tokens.py with --strict and reports PASS as a floor rather than visual sign-off.
Hands visual quality to rendered review instead of claiming that mathematical coherence proves the brand is good.

evals.prompt: Create a design system for a new product. We have no brand, palette, typography, or visual guidelines yet—only a product brief.
evals.expected_output: Does not force brand-to-system without a brand artifact and routes to ui-design-system Create mode.
expectations: Recognises that there is no machine-readable visual brand to derive from.
Routes to ui-design-system Create mode rather than inventing a brand artifact silently.
Does not claim that a product brief alone is sufficient input for deterministic brand derivation.

evals.prompt: Derive our system from this brand JSON. It requires a dark ground and neutral chroma 0.12. Please make reasonable guesses if the tool does not support it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses unsupported dark-ground and out-of-band neutral derivation rather than guessing, and names the required next capability.
expectations: Refuses dark-ground derivation because the current deriver only supports light grounds.
Flags neutral chroma 0.12 as outside the accepted 0.002–0.08 band.
Does not silently clamp, invert or substitute the supplied brand values.
Explains that the missing dark-ground derivation must be implemented or the brand input amended before generation.
